note: Journal prompts attached to every delivered fact. Each is grounded in a named behaviour-change mechanism rather than generic reflection. Placeholders: {move} = the fact's Tonight's 1% Move, {truth} = its Root Truth, {category} = its category. Prompts rotate on their own cycle, independent of the fact rotation, so the same fact rarely arrives with the same question twice.

mechanisms.implementation_intention: Gollwitzer. Specifying when/where/how roughly doubles follow-through versus intention alone. The strongest single effect in the literature.
mechanisms.identity: Clear. Anchoring the behaviour to self-concept rather than outcome, so it survives low motivation.
mechanisms.elaborative_interrogation: Asking why a fact matters to you specifically. Deepens encoding and makes the reason personally retrievable later.
mechanisms.prospective_regret: Loss framing against a concrete future moment. Losses move people more than equivalent gains.
mechanisms.mental_contrasting: Oettingen's WOOP. Pairing the desired outcome with the real obstacle beats visualising success alone.
mechanisms.anchoring: Fogg. Attaching a tiny new behaviour to an existing reliable one.
mechanisms.self_efficacy: Bandura. Recalling a past success is the strongest source of belief that you can do it again.
mechanisms.attribution: Separating what you controlled from what you did not, so a bad night does not become evidence of failure.
mechanisms.commitment: Converting a vague intention into a stated commitment raises follow-through.
mechanisms.episodic_future_thinking: Vividly simulating the future self who benefits, which makes the delayed reward feel present.
mechanisms.minimum_viable: Defining the floor version you would do on your worst night, so the streak never fully breaks.

prompts.text: Name the exact moment tonight this is most likely to break. Finish the sentence: When ______ happens, I will ______.
Where will you physically be at 9:00 PM tonight, and what will your hands be doing? Be specific.
Pick the time you will do this, not the intention. What time, exactly?
Finish this: someone who genuinely sleeps like a top 1% operator would, right now, ______.
Which version of yourself did today's choices vote for? The operator, or the one who stays up?
Say it in the present tense, not the future: I am someone who ______.
Why does this one actually matter to you? Not in general. To you, this week.
What does this make you think about last night specifically?
Where have you already seen this play out in your own body? Give one real example.
If you ignore this tonight, name the specific cost tomorrow. Not vague tiredness — the actual thing you will do worse.
What will you have traded away by 11:30 PM if nothing changes tonight?
Who gets the worse version of you tomorrow if tonight goes badly?
Best case if you hold this for 30 nights — then, immediately, the single obstacle most likely to stop you tonight.
What is the one thing most likely to push tonight's bedtime? Name it now, while you can still act on it.
Anchor it to something you already do without thinking. Finish: After I ______, I will ______.
What existing habit could carry this one on its back?
Name one night this month you got this exactly right. What made it work?
What is the longest streak you have held on this? What broke it?
Last night's result — how much was inside your control and how much was not? Be honest about the split.
Name one thing you controlled well last night, and one you did not. No self-criticism, just the data.
State it as a commitment, not an intention. Write the actual sentence you would be embarrassed to break.
What time tonight is genuinely non-negotiable? Commit to it in writing, right now.
Picture 6:30 AM tomorrow having done this tonight. What is concretely different about that version of the morning?
Picture yourself a year from now having held this. What has compounded?
What would you have to stop doing to make this automatic instead of effortful?
What friction is standing between you and this move? Remove one piece of it tonight.
What is the 30-second version of this move — the one you would still do on your worst night?
Set the floor, not the ceiling. What is the smallest version of this that still counts?

intake.request:
Log last night before the day starts. Reply with your sleep score, and optionally hours slept and how you feel 1-5.

Examples:
  84
  84 7.5
  84 7.5 4

The ring already knows. Writing it down yourself is the point.

Finish it: today I am someone who ______.
